text:
Re-read after 0.54.1. 17 tests. The confirms below went stale because the error contracts in this file changed.

What changed and why: an unresolved ref used to print and RETURN, exiting 0, so a script could not tell a miss from a hit. Both affected tests now assert SystemExit with code 1. One of them previously ended in `assert "no entity" in out(capsys) or True` - which asserted nothing at all, since `or True` cannot fail. It now asserts the message and the exit code.

Added in the same pass: test_meta_ambiguous_ref_names_the_candidates, covering the other branch of _resolve_error. A bare name matching several entities used to answer "no entity matches", a false negative that sends a caller to grep when the map knows five and needed one word of disambiguation. That test skips rather than lying if the fixture happens to contain no ambiguous short name - a skip is honest, a vacuous pass is not.

The module docstring's claim that error contracts are asserted via SystemExit is now true of more of the file than when it was written; keep it that way, and be suspicious of any assertion in here ending in `or True`.

author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.1. SUPERSEDES the confirm below on one point and upholds the rest.

That entry defended test_meta_ambiguous_ref_names_the_candidates skipping when the fixture contains no ambiguous short name: "a skip is honest, a vacuous pass is not." Correct as far as it goes, and it is why the test was written that way. But it has been skipping ever since - the fixture never had a duplicate short name - so the branch it exists to cover was never once executed. An honest skip is still zero coverage, and this was zero coverage of the specific branch whose absence cost 0.55.5 and 0.56.0: reporting a refusal as a gap. Found by `-rs`, not by any failure, because a skip is silent by design.

Fixed by making the fixture contain the case rather than by removing the skip: src/shop.py now declares Aisle.restock and Depot.restock, so `restock` is ambiguous and the assertion runs. The skip stays as the guard it was meant to be. Falsified - reverting query.py:283 to "no entity matches" fails the test.

The rule that generalises: a conditional skip guarding a fixture property must be paired with a fixture that HAS the property, or the guard silently becomes the outcome. The remaining claims below still hold - SystemExit with code 1 on both error contracts, no assertion ending in `or True`, and the module docstring accurate. Count is now 16 tests, none skipped.
